reviewer_role: Non-author of P7-017 seccomp guard, descendant trace parser and offline archive auditor. Earlier source review is supplemented here by actual fixed-source execution receipts and raw original tool observations.
method: Read three exact archived receipts plus both original per-profile matrix observation JSON files through the official connector. Independently recomputed configuration/process/trace/IPC totals and checked feature, binary, source, tool, cache, exit and kernel-positive-control identities using JavaScript assertions. The full descendant parser and all ZIP streams were actually replayed by the separately reviewed CI auditor; this reviewer did not re-run a second complete syscall parser locally.
decisions: Both actual Cargo feature profiles are exact: default features [], semantic features ['semantic']; neither enables semantic-http.
All four zero-key initial configurations execute the same full 14-tool list; all four perform real reopen/persistence checks, and semantic cache absence is retained.
Zero external attempts follows complete descendant trace replay, not exit code zero alone. Original observations deliberately retain network_socket_attempts=null until joined to the trace evidence.
Eight observed anonymous AF_UNIX STREAM pairs have reciprocal kernel inode/peer witnesses. They are disclosed local IPC, not falsely counted as zero socket activity.
IPv4 and IPv6 actual probes terminate SIGSYS; the retained swallowed-child counterexample is rejected from descendant evidence even when the parent exits normally.
Original source/validation bytes, launcher policy, per-process trace checks and tool assertions remain unchanged by the portable identity adaptation.
limitations: This is the declared Linux process-local seccomp plus full strace engineering gate; it is not a proof for arbitrary unobserved future code paths or platforms.
No claim of remote compiler/source-to-binary attestation. The test runner executable is identified by retained Cargo/actual runtime hashes and is not archived as a binary in the original artifact.
No live-provider or held-out semantic benefit evidence is supplied.
Task dependencies and final integrated G7/ledger changes remain owned by root; no tasks or refs were modified by this review.
